en: n. the act of copying someone or something; a copy of something, especially something expensive; a. made to look like something more expensive
ex: The shop sells cheap imitations of famous brands.
那家店賣著知名品牌的廉價仿冒品。
ph: imitation is the sincerest form of flattery

en: n. a long tube made of rubber or plastic used for carrying water; (old) a long stocking; vt. to wash or water something using a hose
ex: He used a hose to water the garden.
他用水管替花園澆水。

en: n. a natural substance such as gold, iron or salt that is dug from the ground; an element that the body needs, such as calcium or iron; (British) a soft drink; a. relating to substances that are not living
ex: Calcium is an important mineral for strong bones.
鈣是強健骨骼的重要礦物質。

en: a. enough or good enough for a particular purpose; acceptable but not excellent
ex: Make sure you get adequate sleep before the exam.
考試前務必睡眠充足。

en: n. very strong anger that is difficult to control; a strong wish for something; a fashionable thing; vi. to be very angry; (of a storm or fire) to continue with violence
ex: He screamed in rage when he saw the broken window.
他看到破窗時暴怒尖叫。

en: n. drinks such as beer, wine or whisky that can make you drunk; a colorless liquid found in alcoholic drinks; a chemical used as a fuel or solvent
ex: Drinking too much alcohol is bad for your health.
喝太多酒對健康有害。

en: vt. to remember something from the past; to order someone to return; to ask for a product to be returned because of a fault; n. the act of remembering; an order to return something
ex: I can't recall where I put my keys.
我想不起來把鑰匙放在哪了。

en: n. the act of changing words from one language into another; a piece of writing that has been translated; the process of changing something into another form
ex: The translation of the novel took two years.
這本小說的翻譯花了兩年。

en: vt. to have something in your mind as a plan or purpose; to mean something to be used for a particular purpose; to want something to be understood in a particular way
ex: I intend to finish this report by tomorrow.
我打算明天前完成這份報告。

en: n. information or data put into a computer; the amount of time, effort or ideas that someone contributes; the power or signal that goes into a machine; vt. to put data into a computer
ex: We would welcome your input on the new design.
我們歡迎你對新設計提供意見。

en: n. the act of decorating something; something used to make a place or thing look more attractive; a medal given for bravery
ex: The Christmas tree was covered with colorful decorations.
聖誕樹上掛滿了色彩繽紛的裝飾品。

en: a. extremely important or necessary; relating to life; full of life and energy; (of a body part) necessary to stay alive
ex: It is vital that you take your medicine every day.
每天服藥非常重要。

en: n. a strong connection between people; an agreement; a certificate issued by a government or company to borrow money; a chemical force that holds atoms together; vt. to stick two things together; vi. to form a close connection with someone
ex: A strong bond developed between the two friends.
這兩位朋友之間建立了牢固的情誼。

en: n. the ability to develop or achieve something in the future; the possibility that something will happen; a. possible in the future; capable of becoming something
ex: The young athlete has great potential.
這位年輕運動員潛力十足。

en: vt. to formally give up a job or position; to accept something unpleasant without complaining; vi. to leave a job or position
ex: He resigned from his position as manager last week.
他上週辭去了經理的職位。

en: n. (witch) a woman who is believed to have magic powers; (wizard) a man with magic powers; vt. to cast a spell on someone; to attract or charm someone
ex: The witch in the fairy tale cast a spell on the prince.
童話中的女巫對王子施了咒語。

en: n. the study or work of designing and building machines, roads, bridges and other structures; the use of skill to design or build something; the act of skillfully arranging something
ex: She studied engineering at a university in Taipei.
她在台北的一所大學學工程。

en: a. causing trouble, annoyance or difficulty; difficult to deal with
ex: The troublesome cough kept him awake all night.
那惱人的咳嗽讓他整晚睡不著。

en: adv. used to introduce more exact information about something you have just mentioned; used when you want to explain what you mean by a statement
ex: Two students, namely Tom and Mary, were absent.
兩位學生，即湯姆和瑪麗，缺席了。

en: n. the art or process of taking photographs; the activity of taking photographs as a hobby or job
ex: She has been interested in photography since she was a teenager.
她從青少年時期就對攝影有興趣。

en: n. a device that produces electricity to power things such as toys, clocks or cars; the crime of hitting someone; a large group of guns used in an army; a set of tests
ex: The phone battery ran out of power.
手機電池沒電了。

en: vt. to take something quickly and firmly; to take something by force or legal authority; to take an opportunity; vi. to suddenly stop working or become stuck
ex: Police seized a large amount of illegal drugs at the border.
警方在邊境查獲大量非法毒品。

en: vt. to give something up to someone else; to give up control of something; vi. to stop fighting and admit defeat; n. the act of giving up or giving in
ex: The army had to surrender after a long siege.
經過長期圍困，軍隊不得不投降。

en: n. a serious argument or disagreement; a disagreement between two groups, such as workers and employers; vt. to argue about something; to question whether something is true; vi. to argue with someone
ex: The two countries are in a dispute over the border.
兩國正為邊界問題起爭端。

en: n. a sentence or phrase taken from a book or speech; the act of repeating someone's words; a price for a job or service; a stock market price
ex: The essay included a quotation from Shakespeare.
這篇文章引用了莎士比亞的一句話。

en: vi. to shake slightly because you are afraid, cold or nervous; (of something) to move slightly; to feel very worried about something; n. a shaking movement of the body or voice
ex: Her hands trembled as she opened the letter.
她打開信時雙手顫抖。

en: a. happening by chance and not intended; not planned; of secondary importance; n. a sign in music that raises or lowers a note
ex: It was an accidental discovery that led to a new medicine.
這項意外的發現促成了一種新藥。

en: a. very pleasant and enjoyable; giving a lot of pleasure; charming
ex: We spent a delightful afternoon in the garden.
我們在花園裡度過了愉快的下午。

en: n. a dried grape, often used in cooking and baking
ex: She added raisins to the oatmeal cookies.
她在燕麥餅乾裡加了葡萄乾。

en: vt. to leave someone or something completely; to stop doing something before it is finished; to stop supporting or believing in something; n. a feeling of complete freedom with no worry about the results
ex: They had to abandon the car because it broke down.
車子拋錨後，他們不得不棄車。

en: vt. to take in a liquid, gas or other substance; to learn and understand new information; to take up all your attention and interest; to accept and deal with something such as a cost
ex: The sponge quickly absorbed the spilled water.
海綿很快吸收了灑出來的水。

en: a. existing as an idea rather than as a physical thing; difficult to understand; n. a short summary of a long piece of writing; a work of art that does not show real objects; vt. to summarize something; to take something away
ex: Love is an abstract concept that is hard to define.
愛是一個難以定義的抽象概念。

en: a. relating to education, especially at a college or university; not practical or important in real life; n. a teacher or researcher at a university
ex: He has an excellent academic record at school.
他在學校的學業成績優異。

en: n. the act of accepting something; agreement that something is right or true; the act of receiving something willingly; the feeling that you can live with something
ex: The idea gained wide acceptance among scientists.
這個想法在科學家之間獲得廣泛認可。

en: n. a person whose job is to keep or check financial accounts for a company or person; a person who deals with money matters
ex: Our accountant helps us prepare our tax returns.
我們的會計師協助我們準備報稅。

en: n. the quality of being exact and without mistakes; the ability to do something exactly; the degree to which something is correct
ex: The accuracy of the report was checked by experts.
這份報告的準確度由專家確認過。

en: n. a chemical substance that has a pH lower than seven and can burn or dissolve other substances; (slang) a drug; a. having a sharp, sour taste; (of remarks) bitter and unkind
ex: Vinegar is a weak acid used in cooking.
醋是烹飪中使用的弱酸。

en: n. a person you know but who is not a close friend; knowledge of someone or something; the state of knowing someone slightly
ex: He is just an acquaintance, not a close friend.
他只是個認識的人，不是密友。

en: vt. to get something by buying or being given it; to gain a skill or knowledge by learning; to get something by effort
ex: She acquired a taste for classical music in her youth.
她年輕時培養出對古典樂的喜好。

en: vt. to change something slightly to make it work better; to move something slightly to make it more suitable; vi. to get used to a new situation
ex: You can adjust the volume with this knob.
你可以用這個旋鈕調整音量。
